result.title: FedLoRD: Personalized Federated Learning based on Low-Rank Structures of Model Parameter Differences
result.summary: We propose FedLoRD, a personalized federated learning (PFL) method based on the low-rank structure of the differences between the global and personalized model parameters. PFL is a branch of federated learning that aims to learn models tailored to the local data of each client under biased local data distributions. In its local training, each client learns a personalized model by regularizing the difference between its model parameters and the global ones sent from the server. The regularization function needs to be designed with priors on the model parameter difference; however, the existing PFL methods rely on empirical choices (e.g., $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-norms), which do not take into account the actual characteristics of the difference. The resulting mismatch of priors can lead to suboptimal personalized models. To address this issue, we propose a PFL method whose regularizer is built on an observed characteristic of the model parameter differences: they are approximately low-rank at every layer. In our method, we first formulate a local training problem with nuclear norm regularization on the layer-wise differences. We further rewrite this problem via the factorized representation of the nuclear norm so that it can be efficiently solved by a plain stochastic gradient descent method. Image classification experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedLoRD outperforms several existing PFL methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FedLoRD，一种个性化联邦学习方法：观察到各客户端个性化模型与全局模型参数之差逐层近似低秩，于是对该差值施加核范数正则，并用因子化表示改写以便用普通 SGD 求解，在三个图像分类基准上取得优于既有 PFL 方法的结果。
